paragraphs: German American Bancorp, Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed (symbol: GABC) financial holding company based in Jasper, Indiana. German American, through its banking subsidiary German American Bank, operates 94 banking offices located throughout Indiana (central/southern), Kentucky (northern/central/western), and Ohio (central/southwest). In Columbus, Ohio and Greater Cincinnati, the Company does business as Heartland Bank, a Division of German American Bank. The Company also owns an investment brokerage subsidiary, German American Investment Services, Inc.

Throughout this Report, when we use the term "Company" and "German American", we will usually be referring to the business and affairs (financial and otherwise) of German American Bancorp, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries as a whole. Occasionally, we will refer to the term "German American Bancorp", "Bancorp", "parent company" or "holding company" when we mean to refer to only German American Bancorp, Inc. and the term "Bank" when we mean to refer only to the Company's bank subsidiary.

The Company's lines of business include retail and commercial banking, and wealth management services. Our retail and commercial banking business involves attracting deposits from the general public and using those funds to originate consumer, commercial and agricultural, commercial and agricultural real estate, and residential mortgage loans, primarily in the Company's local markets. These core banking activities also include the sale of residential mortgage loans in the secondary market. Our wealth management services involve providing trust, investment advisory, brokerage and retirement planning services to customers. Financial and other information by segment is included in Note 18 (Segment Information) of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements included in Item 8 of this Report and is incorporated into this Item 1 by reference. Substantially all of the Company's revenues are derived from customers located in, and substantially all of its assets are located in, the United States.
German American Bank Commercial Bank Jasper, IN German American Investment Services, Inc. Retail Brokerage Jasper, IN

On February 1, 2025, German American Bancorp completed its previously announced acquisition of Heartland BancCorp ("Heartland") through the merger of Heartland with and into the Bancorp. Immediately following completion of the Heartland holding company merger, Heartland's subsidiary bank, Heartland Bank, was merged with and into the Bancorp's subsidiary bank, German American Bank. Heartland, headquartered in Whitehall, Ohio, operated 20 retail banking offices located in Columbus, Ohio and Greater Cincinnati. As of the closing of the transaction, Heartland had total assets of approximately $1.94 billion, total loans of approximately $1.58 billion, and total deposits of approximately $1.73 billion. German American Bancorp issued approximately 7.74 million shares of its common stock, and paid approximately $23.1 million in cash, in exchange for all of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock of Heartland and in cancellation of all options to acquire Heartland common stock outstanding as of the effective time of the merger. For further information regarding this merger and acquisition transaction, see Note 20 (Business Combinations, Goodwill and Intangible Assets) in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements included in Item 8 of this Report, which Note 20 is incorporated into this Item 1 by reference.

During June and July 2024, the Company undertook a partial restructuring of its securities portfolio by selling available-for-sale securities totaling approximately $375.3 million in book value, at an after-tax loss of approximately $27.2 million. The tax-

equivalent yield on the bonds sold was approximately 3.12% with a duration of approximately 7 years. The proceeds from the securities sold were reinvested in the securities portfolio by the end of the third quarter of 2024.

Effective June 1, 2024, German American Insurance, Inc. ("GAI"), a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Bank, sold substantially all of its assets to The Hilb Group of Indiana, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Hilb"), for a purchase price of $40.0 million in cash. As part of the transaction, the Bank, as the parent of GAI, may receive payments for the referral of customers to Hilb, and the Company will refrain from conducting certain insurance activities, in each case, for a period of five (5) years following closing. Prior to the sale, GAI was a full-service agency offering personal and commercial insurance products.

The Company expects to continue to evaluate opportunities to expand its business through opening of new banking, trust, brokerage and financial planning offices, and through acquisitions of other banks, bank branches, portfolios of loans or other assets, and other financial-service-related businesses and assets in the future.
The map below illustrates the locations of the Company's 94 retail and commercial banking, and investment offices.

The industries in which the Company operates are highly competitive. The Bank competes for commercial and retail banking business within its core banking segment not only with financial institutions that have offices in the same counties but also with financial institutions that compete from other locations in Southern Indiana, Kentucky and elsewhere. Further, the Bank competes for loans and deposits not only with commercial banks but also with savings and loan associations, savings banks, credit unions, production credit associations, federal land banks, finance companies, credit card companies, personal loan companies, investment brokerage firms, private equity and debt funds, insurance agencies, insurance companies, lease finance companies, money market funds, mortgage companies, and other non-depository financial intermediaries. There are numerous alternative providers (including national providers that advertise extensively and provide their services via e-mail, direct mail, telephone and the Internet) for trust and financial planning services offered by the Bank and the brokerage products and financial planning services offered by German American Investment Services, Inc. In addition, financial technology, or "FinTech," companies continue their rapid growth into key areas of banking. Many of these competitors have substantially greater resources than the Company.

At February 20, 2026, the Company and its subsidiaries employed approximately 984 full-time equivalent employees. There are no collective bargaining agreements, and we consider employee relations to be good.

People come first at German American. It is through our employees, and their ties to the local community, that we are able to proudly support the communities we serve. We are deeply rooted in these communities. Engrained in our culture is a commitment to give back to the individuals, families, and businesses in our communities. We have a long history of community involvement, from both a contributory standpoint and a dedication to hands-on volunteer efforts. We believe that service to our communities, customers and each other is fun, rewarding and powerful.

German American strives to attract, develop, and retain talented individuals in every community we serve. We understand that, in order to deliver the best financial products and services to our clients, we need to invest in our team's personal and professional success, which includes helping to create a work/life balance and providing further growth opportunities. As a result, our employees have demonstrated a desire and determination to succeed. Our culture encourages them to take initiative, accept challenges, and be collaborative to achieve performance and operating excellence for our customers, shareholders, and communities. German American's reputation relies on integrity. Our team trusts each other in words and actions, which enables our customers to trust our brand. We value honesty, transparency, and diverse perspectives with high ethical standards in all we do.

paragraphs: The following describes some of the principal risks and uncertainties to which our industry in general, and our securities, assets and businesses specifically, are subject; other risks are briefly identified in our cautionary statement that is included under the heading "Forward-Looking Statements and Associated Risks" in Part I, Item 1, "Business." Although we seek ways to manage these risks and uncertainties and to develop programs to control those that we can, we ultimately cannot predict the future. Future results may differ materially from past results, and from our expectations and plans.
Economic weakness in our geographic markets could negatively affect us.

We conduct business from offices that are located throughout Indiana (central/southern), Kentucky (northern/central/western), and Ohio (central/southwest), from which substantially all of our customer base is drawn. Because of the geographic concentration of our operations and customer base, our results depend largely upon economic conditions in these areas. A favorable business environment is generally characterized by, among other factors, economic growth, low inflation, low unemployment, high business and investor confidence, strong business earnings, and efficient capital markets. Unfavorable or uncertain economic and market conditions can be caused by a decline in economic growth in the markets where we operate and in the United States as a whole; declines in business activity or investor or business confidence; limitations on the availability of or increases in the cost of credit and capital; increases in inflation or interest rates; high unemployment; commodity price volatility; natural disasters; or a combination of these or other factors.

Changes in trade policies by the United States or other countries, including tariffs or retaliatory tariffs, may cause inflation, which could impact the prices of products sold or purchased by our borrowers or the demand for their products, negatively impacting their profitability and ability to repay loans. The financial markets and the global economy may also be adversely affected by the current or anticipated impact of military conflict, which events could increase volatility in commodity and energy prices, and raise the possibility of supply disruptions.

Current economic conditions continue to be impacted by inflation rates that persistently remain above the Federal Reserve's target rate and by elevated interest rates. A prolonged period of higher inflation may impact our profitability by negatively impacting our fixed costs and expenses. Economic and inflationary pressure on consumers and uncertainty regarding economic improvement could have direct or indirect material adverse impacts on us, on our customers or on the financial institutions with whom we deal as counterparties to financial transactions. Such pressures could negatively impact customers' ability to obtain new loans or to repay existing loans, diminish the values of any collateral securing such loans and could cause increases in the number of the Company's customers experiencing financial distress and in the levels of the Company's delinquencies, non-

performing loans and other problem assets, charge-offs and provision for credit losses, all of which could materially adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations. The underwriting and credit monitoring policies and procedures that we have adopted cannot eliminate the risk that we might incur losses on account of factors relating to the economy like those identified above, and those losses could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

Net income for the year ended December 31, 2025 totaled $112,635,000, or $3.06 per share, an increase of $28,824,000, or approximately 8% on a per share basis, from the year ended December 31, 2024 net income of $83,811,000, or $2.83 per share. The year ended December 31, 2025 results of operations included Heartland acquisition-related expenses of $6,996,000 ($5,418,000, on an after-tax basis) and the "Day 2" provision for credit losses under the CECL methodology of $16,200,000 ($12,150,000, on an after-tax basis), as well as a net gain on the redemption of subordinated debentures.

Net income for the year ended December 31, 2024 totaled $83,811,000, or $2.83 per share, a decline of $2,077,000, or approximately 3% on a per share basis, from the year ended December 31, 2023 net income of $85,888,000, or $2.91 per share. Net income for the year ended December 31, 2024 included merger-related transaction costs associated with the Company's merger with Heartland that totaled approximately $1,370,000, $1,082,000 after-tax, or $0.04 per share.

Net income for the year ended December 31, 2024 was impacted by the sale of substantially all of the assets of GAI during the second quarter of 2024. The all-cash sale price totaled $40.0 million and resulted in an after-tax gain, net of transaction costs, of approximately $27,476,000, or $0.93 per share. GAI net income, excluding the after-tax gain, contributed approximately $767,000, or $0.03 per share, during 2024 compared with net income of $1,639,000, or $0.06 per share, during the full year of 2023.

Net income for the year ended December 31, 2024 was also impacted by the securities portfolio restructuring transaction whereby available-for-sale securities totaling approximately $375.3 million in book value were sold. The approximate loss on these securities totaled $34,893,000, $27,189,000 after tax, or $0.92 per share, and was included in earnings for the second quarter of 2024. The proceeds from the securities sold were reinvested in the securities portfolio by the end of the third quarter of 2024.

On an adjusted basis, net income for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $129,684,000, or $3.52 per share, compared with adjusted net income of $83,839,000, or $2.83 per share, for the year ended December 31, 2024. Adjusted net income and adjusted earnings per share are non-GAAP financial measures. Refer to "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" contained in this release for additional information, including a reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures.

paragraphs: German American Bancorp, Inc. 為納斯達克上市（代碼：GABC）的金融控股公司，總部設於印第安那州賈斯珀。German American 透過其銀行子公司 German American Bank，於印第安那州（中部/南部）、肯塔基州（北部/中部/西部）及俄亥俄州（中部/西南部）設有 94 家銀行分行。在俄亥俄州哥倫布市及大辛辛那提地區，本公司以 Heartland Bank 為名營運，為 German American Bank 的分公司。本公司亦擁有投資經紀子公司 German American Investment Services, Inc。

於本報告中，當我們使用 "Company" 及 "German American" 這兩個詞時，通常是指 German American Bancorp, Inc. 及其合併子公司整體的業務與事務（財務及其他方面）。偶爾我們會使用 "German American Bancorp"、"Bancorp"、"母公司" 或 "控股公司" 這幾個詞，意指僅指 German American Bancorp, Inc.，而使用 "Bank" 這個詞則意指僅指本公司之銀行子公司。

本公司的業務線包括零售與商業銀行，以及資產管理服務。我們的零售與商業銀行業務涉及從一般大眾吸收存款，並運用這些資金發放消費者、商業及農業貸款、商業及農業不動產貸款以及住宅抵押貸款，主要在本公司當地市場。這些核心銀行業務亦包括在二級市場出售住宅抵押貸款。我們的資產管理服務涉及為客戶提供信託、投資顧問、經紀及退休規劃服務。各業務分部的財務及其他資訊請參閱本報告第 8 項所附之合併財務報表附註第 18 項（分部資訊）並納入本項目 1 作為參考。本公司幾乎所有的收入均來自美國境內的客戶，且幾乎所有的資產均位於美國境內。
German American Bank Commercial Bank Jasper, IN German American Investment Services, Inc. 零售經紀賈斯珀, IN

2025 年 2 月 1 日，德國美國銀行控股公司完成其先前宣佈的收購 Heartland 銀行控股公司（"Heartland"）的交易，透過 Heartland 與德國美國銀行控股公司合併的方式進行。在 Heartland 持股公司合併完成後，Heartland 的子公司銀行 Heartland 銀行與德國美國銀行控股公司的子公司銀行德國美國銀行合併。Heartland 董事會設於俄亥俄州 Whitehall，於俄亥俄州哥倫布市及大辛辛那提地區經營 20 間零售銀行分行。交易完成時，Heartland 的總資產約為 1.94 十億美元，總貸款約為 1.58 十億美元，總存款約為 1.73 十億美元。德國美國銀行控股公司發行約 7.74 百萬股其普通股，並支付約 23.1 百萬美元現金，以換取 Heartland 全部已發行及流通的普通股，並取消截至合併生效時間點所有尚未兌換的 Heartland 普通股選擇權。有關此合併與收購交易之進一步資訊，請參閱本報告第 8 項所附之財務會計彙編說明書附註 20（企業合併、商譽及無形資產），該附註已納入本項目之參考內容。
2024年6月及7月期間，本公司進行部分證券投資組合的重整，出售總計約375.3百萬美元的可供出售證券，產生約27.2百萬美元的稅後損失。稅後收益率為約3.12%，久期為約7年。出售證券所得金額於2024年第三季結束前已重新投資於證券投資組合。
所售債券的相當收益率約為 3.12%，久期約為 7 年。所售證券的所得金額於 2024 年第三季結束前已重新投資於證券投資組合。

2024年6月1日，德國美國保險公司（"GAI"），為銀行的 wholly-owned 子公司，將其幾乎所有資產出售給Indiana的The Hilb Group of Indiana, LLC，為一家德拉瓦州有限責任公司（"Hilb"），交易價格為40.0百萬美元現金。根據交易條款，銀行作為GAI的母公司，可能在合併後五年內因推薦客戶至Hilb而獲得付款，且本公司將在合併後五年內停止進行某些保險業務活動。在出售前，GAI為一家提供個人及商業保險產品的全服務代理機構。
本公司預期將持續評估擴展業務的機會，包括透過開設新的銀行、信託、證券經紀及財務規劃辦事處，以及未來透過收購其他銀行、銀行分行、貸款組合或其他資產，以及其他與金融服務相關的業務及資產。
下圖說明本公司 94 間零售及商業銀行與投資辦事處的所在地。

本公司所從事的產業具有高度競爭性。銀行在其核心銀行業務中，不僅與在相同縣市設有分行的金融機構競爭，也與來自美國印第安納州南部、肯塔基州及其他地區的金融機構競爭。此外，銀行在貸款與存款業務上，不僅與商業銀行競爭，也與儲蓄貸款協會、儲蓄銀行、信用合作社、生產信貸協會、聯邦土地銀行、金融公司、信用卡公司、個人貸款公司、投資證券經紀公司、私人股權與債務基金、保險機構、保險公司、租賃金融公司、貨幣市場基金、房貸公司及其他非存款性金融中介機構競爭。此外，許多替代性服務提供者（包括廣為廣告宣傳並透過電子郵件、直郵、電話及互聯網提供服務的全國性服務提供者）也提供銀行所提供的信託與財務規劃服務，以及德國美國投資服務公司所提供的證券產品與財務規劃服務。此外，金融科技，或稱「FinTech」公司，持續快速成長至銀行業務的關鍵領域。許多這些競爭對手擁有遠較本公司為多的資源。
截至 2026 年 2 月 20 日，本公司及其子公司約僱用 984 名全職等效員工。並無集體談判協議，我們認為員工關係良好。
德國美國公司將員工視為最重要的資產。正是透過我們的員工及其與當地社區的連結，我們才能自豪地支持我們所服務的社區。我們深深紮根於這些社區。我們的文化中內化了對回饋社區個人、家庭與企業的承諾。我們有長期參與社區的歷史，從捐贈的角度與投入實質志工努力的立場。我們相信服務社區、客戶與彼此是一種樂趣、回報且強大的行動。

德國美國公司致力於吸引、培養並留住每一個我們服務社區中的優秀人才。我們瞭解，為了為客戶提供最佳的金融產品與服務，我們需要投資於團隊個人與專業的成功，這包括協助創造工作與生活的平衡，並提供進一步的成長機會。因此，我們的員工已展現出追求成功的渴望與決心。我們的文化鼓勵他們主動發起行動、接受挑戰並協作合作，以實現為客戶、股東與社區帶來卓越表現與運營效率。德國美國公司的聲譽建立在誠信之上。我們的團隊在言語與行動上彼此信任，這使得客戶能信任我們的品牌。我們重視誠實、透明與多元觀點，並在所有行動中維持高道德標準。

paragraphs: German American Bancorp, Inc. 為納斯達克上市 (代碼: GABC) 的金融控股公司，總部設於印第安那州賈斯珀。German American 透過其銀行子公司 German American Bank，於印第安那州 (中部/南部)、肯塔基州 (北部/中部/西部) 和俄亥俄州 (中部/西南部) 運營 94 家銀行分行。在俄亥俄州哥倫布市及大辛辛那提地區，本公司以 Heartland Bank 為名經營業務，為 German American Bank 的一個部門。本公司亦擁有投資經紀子公司 German American Investment Services, Inc.

在本 Management's Discussion and Analysis 中，以及本報告其他地方，當我們使用 "Company" 和 "German American" 這兩個詞時，通常是指本公司及其子公司和附屬公司的業務與事務 (財務及其他方面)。有時，我們會使用 "German American Bancorp"、"Bancorp"、"母公司" 或 "控股公司" 這幾個詞，意指僅指 German American Bancorp, Inc.，而使用 "Bank" 這個詞時，意指僅指本公司銀行子公司。

本 Management's Discussion and Analysis 包含對本公司 2023 至 2025 年度營運主要組成部分的分析，以及 2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2025 年 12 月 31 日的財務狀況。此資訊應與本報告其他地方所附的合併財務報表及腳註，以及本報告第 1 項所載的業務描述 (包括 "展望性陳述與相關風險" 的警示聲明) 一併閱讀。按分部提供的財務及其他資訊，請參閱本報告第 8 項所附合併財務報表腳註中的第 18 項 (分部資訊)，並已納入本第 7 項中。

本 Management's Discussion and Analysis 中所載的管理層對本公司未來營運及表現的預期與目標，以及本第 7 項其他部分的相關內容，均為展望性陳述。讀者應注意，這些展望性陳述是基於假設，並受風險、不確定性及其他因素影響。實際結果可能與本公司所表達或暗示的展望性陳述所預期的結果有重大差異。本第 7 項，以及本報告第 1 項 ("業務") 中標題為 "展望性陳述與相關風險" 的討論，以及第 1A 項 ("風險因素") 的討論 (這些討論已納入本第 7 項中)，列出了一些可能導致本公司實際結果與任何相關展望性陳述所表達或暗示的結果有重大差異的因素。

本 Management's Discussion and Analysis 中所載的管理層對本公司未來營運及表現的預期與目標，以及未來財務狀況、流動性及資本資源的相關資訊，以及本第 7 項其他部分的相關內容，均為展望性陳述。讀者應注意，這些展望性陳述是基於假設，並受風險、不確定性及其他因素影響。實際結果可能與本公司所表達或暗示的展望性陳述所預期的結果有重大差異。本第 7 項，以及本報告第 1 項 ("業務") 中標題為 "展望性陳述與相關風險" 的討論，以及第 1A 項 ("風險因素") 的討論 (這些討論已納入本第 7 項中)，列出了一些可能導致本公司實際結果與任何相關展望性陳述所表達或暗示的結果有重大差異的因素。

於 2025 年 9 月 15 日，Bancorp 以本金金額 100% 加計累積未付利息之價格贖回 Heartland 5.0% 固定轉浮動利率次級債券，到期日為 2030 年，總發行本金金額為 24.3 百萬美元。於 2025 年 12 月 30 日，本公司以本金金額 100% 加計累積未付利息之價格贖回 4.5% 固定轉浮動利率次級債券，到期日為 2029 年，總發行本金金額為 40.0 百萬美元。有關這些贖回之進一步資訊，請參閱本報告第 8 項「合併財務報表附註」中之附註 8（FHLB 借款及其他借款），該附註已納入本項目之參考內容。
2024 年 6 月及 7 月期間，本公司執行了證券投資組合的部分重整，出售了帳面價值總計約 375.3 百萬美元之可供出售證券，產生約 27.2 百萬美元之稅後損失。所售債券之稅後等價報酬率約為 3.12%，久期約為 7 年。所出售證券之所得於 2024 年第三季結束前已重新投資於證券投資組合。

自2024年6月1日起，德國美國保險公司（"GAI"），為本行之 wholly-owned subsidiary，將其幾乎所有資產出售給印第安納州希爾布公司（Hilb），為一家德拉瓦州有限責任公司（"Hilb"），交易對價為40.0 百萬美元現金。此交易中，本行作為GAI之母公司，可能因客戶轉介至Hilb而獲得付款，且本公司將於交易完成後五年（5）年內，避免從事特定保險業務。出售前，GAI為提供個人及商業保險產品之全服務代理機構。有關此交易之進一步資訊，請參見本報告第8項所附財務會計彙編附註中之附註2（保險資產出售）。

2025年12月31日財年淨收入為112,635,000美元，每股為3.06美元，較2024年12月31日財年淨收入83,811,000美元，每股2.83美元，增加28,824,000美元，每股增加約8%。2025年12月31日財年營運結果包含與Heartland收購相關的費用6,996,000美元（稅後5,418,000美元），以及根據CECL方法計算的"Day 2"信貸損失準備金16,200,000美元（稅後12,150,000美元），以及子公司可轉換債券兌換所產生的淨收益。
2024年12月31日財年淨收入為83,811,000美元，每股為2.83美元，較2023年12月31日財年淨收入85,888,000美元，每股為2.91美元，每股減少約3%，即減少2,077,000美元。2024年12月31日財年淨收入包含與本公司與Heartland合併相關之交易費用約1,370,000美元，稅後為1,082,000美元，每股為0.04美元。

2024 年截至 12 月 31 日的淨收入受到 2024 年第二季出售 GAI 大部分資產的影響。該筆全現金買賣總價為 40.0 百萬美元，並產生扣除交易成本後的稅後獲利約 27,476,000 美元，或每股 0.93 美元。排除稅後獲利後，GAI 的淨收入在 2024 年貢獻約 767,000 美元，或每股 0.03 美元，與 2023 年全年淨收入 1,639,000 美元，或每股 0.06 美元相比。
2024年12月31日財年淨收入亦受證券投資組合重組交易之影響，該交易出售總計約375.3 百萬美元帳面價值之可供出售證券。這些證券之損失約為34,893,000美元，稅後為27,189,000美元，每股為0.92美元，並於2024年第二季納入營收。出售證券所得於2024年第三季結束前已重新投資於證券投資組合。
調整後之2025年12月31日財年淨收入為129,684,000美元，每股為3.52美元，與2024年12月31日財年調整後淨收入83,839,000美元，每股為2.83美元相比。調整後淨收入與調整後每股盈餘為非GAAP財務指標。有關非GAAP財務指標之使用，請參閱本公告中所附之"非GAAP財務指標之使用"，包含非GAAP財務指標與最直接可比較GAAP財務指標之對應關係。

paragraphs: 以下說明了我們產業在整體上，以及我們證券、資產與業務在特定方面所面臨的一些主要風險與不確定性；其他風險則在本節第 1 項「業務」標題下所附的「預測性陳述與相關風險」警示聲明中簡要提及。儘管我們尋求方法來管理這些風險與不確定性，並發展計畫來控制我們所能控制的風險，但我們最終無法預測未來。未來的結果可能與過去的結果以及我們的預期與計畫有重大差異。
我們地理市場的經濟疲弱可能會對我們產生負面影響。

我們的業務從印第安那州（中部/南部）、肯塔基州（北部/中部/西部）以及俄亥俄州（中部/西南部）的辦公室進行，而我們的客戶羣體幾乎全部來自這些地區。由於我們的業務與客戶羣體地理集中，我們的結果 largely 取決於這些地區的經濟狀況。有利的商業環境通常特徵為，包括經濟成長、低通貨膨脹、低失業率、高企業與投資者信心、強勁企業獲利以及有效率的資本市場。不利或不確定的經濟與市場條件可能由我們經營的市場以及美國整體經濟成長率下降所引起；商業活動或投資者與企業信心下降；信貸與資本可得性的限制或成本增加；通貨膨脹或利率上升；高失業率；商品價格波動；天然災害；或這些因素或其他因素的組合所造成。
美國或其他國家的貿易政策變動，包括關稅或報復性關稅，可能會導致通貨膨脹，這可能會影響我們借款人的產品售出或購入價格，或影響其產品的需求，從而對其利潤率與償還貸款的能力產生負面影響。目前或預期的軍事衝突影響，也可能對金融市場與全球經濟產生不利影響，這些事件可能增加商品與能源價格的波動性，並提高供應中斷的可能性。

目前的經濟狀況持續受到通貨膨脹率持續高於聯邦儲備理事會目標利率以及利率偏高的影響。較長時間的高通貨膨脹可能會透過對我們固定成本與費用產生負面影響，而影響我們的利潤率。對消費者與經濟改善的不確定性，可能會對我們、我們的客戶或我們交易的金融機構產生直接或間接的重大負面影響。這些壓力可能會影響客戶取得新貸款或償還現有貸款的能力，降低用來擔保這些貸款的任何財產價值，並可能導致本公司客戶經歷財務困難的情況數量增加，以及本公司逾期貸款、非表現貸款及其他問題資產、核銷與信貸減損準備金的水準上升，所有這些都可能對我們的財務狀況與營運成果產生重大負面影響。我們所採用的風險評估與信貸監控政策與程序，無法消除我們可能因上述與經濟相關的因素而產生損失的風險，而這些損失可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果與現金流產生重大負面影響。
我們所採用的風險評估與信貸監控政策與程序，無法消除我們可能因上述與經濟相關的因素而產生損失的風險，而這些損失可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果與現金流產生重大負面影響。
